q: What is the primary object of a surprise inspection in Railway accounts?

options.A: To verify correctness of transactions and detect fraud without notice
options.B: To give advance notice of an audit visit
options.C: To train the staff of the office inspected
options.D: To help the office prepare its annual budget

q: Surprise inspections of accounts matters are normally conducted by whom?

options.A: The station master of the station concerned
options.B: Officers of the Personnel Department
options.C: Inspectors of the Accounts internal check organisation

q: The defining feature of a surprise check is that it is:

options.A: Carried out without prior intimation to the office checked
options.B: Conducted only in the presence of the Vigilance Officer
options.C: Announced one week in advance in writing
options.D: Done only after the annual audit is over

q: On a surprise visit to a cash office, the inspector's first step is to:

options.A: Check the personal files of the cashiers
options.B: Close the office for the day
options.C: Ask the cashier to prepare a fresh cash book
options.D: Physically verify cash in hand and compare it with the cash book balance

q: If a shortage of cash is detected during a surprise check, the inspector should:

options.A: Record it and report immediately to the controlling authority for recovery and action
options.B: Ignore it if the amount is small
options.C: Adjust it against the next remittance
options.D: Ask the cashier to make good the loss silently

q: Inspection reports of surprise checks are required to be:

options.A: Kept only in the inspector's personal diary
options.B: Destroyed after the visit is over
options.C: Submitted within the prescribed time to the authority that ordered the check
options.D: Sent directly to the Railway Board in every case

q: Effective follow-up on surprise inspection reports is ensured by:

options.A: Maintaining a register of outstanding inspection paras and watching compliance
options.B: Filing the reports and forgetting them
options.C: Repeating the same check every week
options.D: Publishing the reports in the railway magazine

q: If a surprise check reveals suspected fraud with malafide intent, the proper course is to:

options.A: Let the staff settle it among themselves
options.B: Close the inspection and destroy the notes
options.C: Impose a fine on the spot and close the case
options.D: Report to the higher accounts authority and refer the matter to Vigilance

q: A surprise check of a booking office normally includes:

options.A: Reconciling ticket stock with tickets sold and cash collected
options.B: Checking the punctuality of trains

q: Station cash collections are required to be:

options.A: Kept at the station until month end
options.B: Used for station expenses freely
options.C: Remitted to the bank promptly without undue retention
options.D: Handed over to the train guard

q: Duplicate keys of cash safes are required to be:

options.A: Deposited in safe custody, generally with the bank
options.B: Kept by the cashier at home

q: A surprise check of an imprest account verifies that:

options.A: Cash in hand plus vouchers for expenditure equal the sanctioned imprest amount
options.B: The imprest holder is punctual in attendance
options.C: The imprest is invested to earn interest
options.D: The imprest holder has a personal bank account

q: Cash in the custody of train guards is checked to ensure:

options.A: The cash held reconciles with the cash book and remittances made
options.B: Guards carry no cash at all
options.D: Cash is counted only at headquarters

q: Surprise checks on Ticket Checking staff mainly aim to detect:

options.B: Cleanliness of coaches
options.D: Non-remittance or under-remittance of excess fares and unaccounted receipts

q: Surprise inspection of muster rolls on works is meant to detect:

options.A: Fictitious or inflated labour entries and overpayments
options.B: Overtime worked by supervisors

q: During a surprise check of a stores depot, the inspector verifies:

options.A: Physical stock against bin cards and ledger balances on a test-check basis
options.B: The colour of the depot building
options.C: The home addresses of store keepers

q: Surprise dip checks of fuel oil installations are conducted to:

options.A: Verify physical oil balances against book balances and detect losses
options.B: Check the temperature of the oil
options.C: Test the quality of lubricants only
options.D: Measure the height of the tanks

q: Surprise checks of weighbridges and weighing machines help to detect:

options.A: Under-weighment frauds affecting freight and parcel revenue
options.B: Overloading of wagons only

q: A surprise check of scrap lots before auction verifies that:

options.A: The lots offered agree with the records of scrap generated and held
options.B: The auctioneer is well dressed
options.D: Scrap is sold at fixed government prices

q: Surprise checks of pantry cars and catering units examine:

options.B: The uniform of the waiters
options.C: Cash sales, stock of provisions and licence fee realisation

q: In a parcel office surprise check, the inspector looks for:

options.B: The age of the parcels clerk
options.C: Unbooked or undelivered parcels and unrealised freight
options.D: The size of the office room

q: A surprise check of the luggage office aims to ensure:

options.B: The office opens on time
options.C: Luggage left unclaimed is properly registered and accounted for

q: Surprise verification of ticket machines (UTS/PRS) focuses on:

options.B: The noise made by the printer
options.C: Cash collected matching the machine-generated sales reports
options.D: The colour of the display screen

q: Blank ticket stock is kept under strict control because:

options.B: It fades in sunlight
options.C: Unaccounted blank tickets can be misused to defraud railway revenue

q: Excess Fare Ticket (EFT) books are surprise-checked to verify:

options.B: The colour of the book cover
options.C: That all foils are accounted for and collections remitted

q: During a surprise cash check, fake or defective currency notes found are:

options.B: Mixed with genuine notes
options.C: Recorded, segregated and reported for further action

q: Remittance of station earnings delayed beyond the prescribed period indicates:

options.B: Good relations with the bank
options.C: A possible irregularity inviting a surprise check

q: A cashier's personal cash must be kept:

options.A: Mixed with railway cash for convenience
options.B: In the same safe without record
options.D: Completely separate from railway cash in his custody

q: Surprise checks of paid vouchers in an accounts office aim to detect:

options.B: Use of wrong ink
options.C: Duplicate payments and over-certification of claims

q: Before starting a surprise inspection, the inspector generally carries:

options.A: A letter of introduction to the press
options.B: A camera for publicity
options.C: Proper authority and identification for the check

q: Surprise checks of works measurements verify that:

options.B: Labourers are happy
options.D: Quantities certified for payment agree with actual work executed at site

q: Material-at-site accounts are surprise-checked to ensure:

options.B: The site is fenced
options.D: Materials issued to works are actually available at site and not diverted

q: Surprise inspections are also conducted during night hours because:

options.B: Offices are closed at night
options.C: Trains do not run at night
options.D: Irregularities are more likely when supervision is thin

q: The cloak room is included in surprise checks mainly to verify:

options.B: The design of the receipt
options.D: That articles deposited and cloak room fees are properly accounted for

q: A surprise check of a reservation office examines:

options.B: The queue length
options.D: Cancellation and refund transactions with related cash handling

q: Platform ticket sales are surprise-checked because:

options.B: Platforms are crowded
options.D: Cash sales without a name record are prone to suppression

q: Season ticket renewals are verified in surprise checks to detect:

options.B: Overcrowding in trains
options.D: Issue of season tickets without realising the full fare

q: When an inspector finds only minor procedural lapses, he should:

options.B: Ignore them completely
options.D: Point them out for rectification and record them in the report

q: The interface between surprise inspection and Vigilance arises when:

options.B: Staff are on leave
options.C: Findings indicate malafide, fraud or criminal misconduct

q: A preventive check differs from a surprise inspection in that it is:

options.B: Conducted only by the police
options.D: Aimed at preventing irregularities through guidance rather than detecting committed ones

q: Surprise verification of cash in transit covers:

options.B: Coins in vending machines
options.D: Remittances moving between offices and the bank until acknowledged

q: Bank reconciliation statements are test-checked to ensure:

options.B: Cheques are colourful
options.D: Unadjusted items are genuine timing differences and not misappropriation

q: Surprise checks of lost property offices ensure that:

options.B: Found articles are registered and their disposal accounted for

q: Inspection of oil depots by surprise includes checking:

options.B: Dip readings of tanks against stock books and seals on tank fittings

q: A surprise check diary or programme is maintained to:

options.B: Plan coverage of units and avoid duplication, kept confidential

q: Surprise checks of contractor's bills focus on:

options.B: Measurements, rates and deductions like security deposit and taxes
options.D: The colour of the bill paper

q: Sleeping car and attendant services are surprise-checked for:

options.A: Bedding charges collected and linen stock accounted for
options.B: The colour of blankets

q: Surprise checks of auction sales verify that:

options.B: The highest bid is accepted and sale proceeds fully realised

q: Cash safes are surprise-checked to confirm that:

options.B: The safe contains only railway cash and valuables with proper records

q: A test check of pay bills during surprise inspection looks for:

options.B: Payments to non-existent staff and incorrect allowances

q: Surprise checks of the claims office examine:

options.B: Settlement of compensation claims with proper sanction and documentation

q: When cash is found in excess during a surprise check, the inspector should:

options.B: Distribute it among staff
options.C: Record the excess and investigate its source

q: Surprise checks of refreshment rooms cover:

options.A: The taste of the food only
options.B: Sales accounting, stock of provisions and licence dues

q: The frequency of surprise checks for a unit is generally decided on the basis of:

options.B: Risk, volume of cash handled and past irregularities

q: Surprise inspection of stores issue notes detects:

options.B: Issues made without proper indents or to unauthorised persons

q: During a surprise check, the inspector must avoid:

options.B: Disclosing the programme of future checks to the staff

q: Surprise checks of running room and rest house collections verify:

options.B: Occupancy charges and allied collections against occupancy records

q: A surprise check report should be:

options.B: Factual, specific and supported by evidence collected on the spot

q: Surprise verification of suspense heads of account aims to ensure that:

options.A: Suspense balances are cleared expeditiously and contain no hidden losses
options.B: Suspense accounts earn interest

q: The ultimate test of an effective surprise inspection system is:

options.B: Timely detection of irregularities and their rectification with deterrent effect
